expectation: CAIX or carbonic anhydrase is a membrane or cytoplasmic stain on a subset of tumour or epithelial cells. It should appear in patches, often in hypoxic regions, and be absent from most immune and stromal cells. Expect strong ROI-to-ROI variation.
observed: Whole tissue: 14 ROIs. Several (row 2 col 4, row 3 cols 1–2) show bright yellow network or rim patterns around nuclei-poor spaces. One ROI has a saturated blob at its edge. Most ROIs are dim. B and C show only faint grain with no distinct cells. D is a smeared saturated blob at the image edge.
why: A few ROIs show patchy, rim-like signal that fits heterogeneous membranous staining, but B, C and D give no cell-level evidence and the brightest signal looks like edge artefact.
